critical_growth_stages.importance: Water stress leads to massive square shedding.
Critical for flower retention and pollen viability.
Severe stress causes young boll drop and shorter fiber staple length.

irrigation_methods.drip_irrigation: Inline drip system with 16 mm lateral per crop row, 40-50 cm dripper spacing, 2.0 - 4.0 LPH discharge rate. Operates 2-3 hours every alternate day. Achieves 40-50% water savings and allows fertigation.
irrigation_methods.furrow_irrigation: Alternate furrow irrigation method saves 30-35% water without reducing yield. Irrigate when soil moisture depletes to 50% available water capacity.

water_stress_remedy: If moisture stress occurs during dry spells, give foliar spray of 2% Potassium Nitrate (KNO3 @ 20 g/L) or 1% Urea to reduce leaf senescence and square drop.

critical_growth_stages.importance: Requires 2 cm standing water for root anchor.
Water deficit drastically reduces spikelet number per panicle.
Extreme sensitivity; drought causes spikelet sterility and chaffy ears.
Requires saturated soil; stress causes floret abortion.
Grain filling requires adequate moisture.

irrigation_methods.alternate_wetting_and_drying_awd: Install perforated field water tube (Pani Pipe) of 30 cm length. Re-irrigate to 5 cm depth only when water level inside tube drops to 15 cm below soil surface. Saves 25-30% irrigation water and reduces methane emissions.
irrigation_methods.continuous_flooding: Maintain 2-5 cm shallow standing water during critical reproductive stages.

water_stress_remedy: Drain standing water completely 10-12 days before anticipated harvest to facilitate uniform grain drying and mechanical combine movement.

critical_growth_stages.importance: Light frequent irrigations prevent seedling mortality.
Moisture stress causes flower bud drop.
Deficit causes fruit drop and small distorted pods.

irrigation_methods.drip_irrigation: Paired row planting with 16 mm lateral between two rows; 30 cm dripper spacing with 2 LPH drippers; run 1.5 - 2.5 hours every alternate day.
irrigation_methods.ridge_furrow: Irrigate furrow up to 2/3rd height of ridge to avoid water wetting root crown directly (prevents collar rot).

water_stress_remedy: Avoid water stagnation at all costs; stagnant water for >12 hours triggers immediate root asphyxiation and wilting.

critical_growth_stages.importance: Moderate moisture promotes deep root architecture.
Stress leads to flower drop and poor blossom fertilization.
Irregular watering induces blossom end rot and radial fruit cracking.

irrigation_methods.drip_irrigation_with_mulch: Drip system with silver-black polyethylene mulch (30 micron) reduces crop water demand by 45% and eliminates weed competition.
irrigation_methods.furrow_irrigation: Irrigate every 5-7 days in summer, 8-10 days in winter.

water_stress_remedy: Maintain steady, uniform soil moisture; heavy irrigation after a dry spell is the primary cause of fruit skin cracking.

critical_growth_stages.importance: Most critical irrigation stage in wheat; delay causes 35-40% irreversible yield penalty.
Governs effective ear-bearing tiller number.
Determines floret number per spikelet.
Pollination and fertilization phase.
Affects initial grain filling rate.
Ensures grain test weight and prevents shriveling.

irrigation_methods.border_strip_irrigation: Check basin or border strip (6m x 40m) designed for uniform water spread; apply 60-70 mm depth per irrigation.
irrigation_methods.sprinkler_irrigation: Suitable for undulated topography and light sandy soils; saves 30% water and protects against frost.

water_stress_remedy: If only 1 irrigation available: Apply at CRI (21 DAS). If 2 irrigations: Apply at CRI and Flowering. If 3: CRI, Late Jointing, and Milk stage.

critical_growth_stages.importance: Rapid vegetative growth and ear shoot initiation.
Extreme sensitivity; water stress delays silking relative to pollen shed (ASI - Anthesis Silking Interval expands) causing bare cobs.
Desiccation of silks leads to poor fertilization.
Kernel depth and test weight development.

irrigation_methods.furrow_irrigation: Irrigate in furrows with plants grown on ridges; avoids direct waterlogging of collar roots.
irrigation_methods.drip_irrigation: Inline drip lateral spaced at 60 cm row spacing with fertigation.

water_stress_remedy: Maize cannot tolerate water stagnation for more than 24 hours at knee-high stage; provide instant field drainage channels.

critical_growth_stages.importance: Ensures maximum flower production.
Upper 5 cm soil must remain moist and friable to permit peg penetration without mechanical resistance.
Kernel enlargement; moisture stress causes 'pops' (empty pods).

irrigation_methods.sprinkler_irrigation: Sprinkler system operated in morning or late evening; highly effective for softening soil surface during peg entry.
irrigation_methods.broad_bed_and_furrow: BBF method (beds 120 cm wide, furrows 30 cm) with irrigation through furrows.

water_stress_remedy: Withhold irrigation during early vegetative phase (10-25 DAS) to encourage deeper taproot elongation; resume at flowering.

critical_growth_stages.importance: Moisture deficit causes flower abortion and poor pod set.
Affects seed size, oil concentration, and seed shriveling.

irrigation_methods.broad_bed_furrow_bbf: BBF system facilitates drainage during heavy monsoon cloudbursts and serves as irrigation furrows during dry spells.
irrigation_methods.sprinkler_irrigation: Supplemental sprinkler irrigation during mid-season monsoon dry spells.

water_stress_remedy: If rainfed dry spell exceeds 15 days during pod fill, give 1 protective irrigation of 50 mm.

critical_growth_stages.importance: Prevents floral drop during post-monsoon dry spell.
Critical for bold seed development.

irrigation_methods.protective_irrigation: 1-2 protective furrow irrigations during terminal drought in October-November increase grain yield by 35-50%.

water_stress_remedy: Foliar spray of 2% Urea or 1% KNO3 during dry spells reduces drought-induced shedding.

critical_growth_stages.importance: Branching and floral bud development.
Directly impacts seed weight.

irrigation_methods.light_furrow_irrigation: Apply light irrigation (50-60 mm). Never flood chickpea fields, as excess moisture triggers Fusarium wilt and collar rot.

water_stress_remedy: DO NOT irrigate chickpea during active flowering (50-60 DAS) as it triggers excessive vegetative growth and flower drop.

critical_growth_stages.importance: Promotes secondary branching and siliquae points.
Ensures full seed formation and oil synthesis.

irrigation_methods.sprinkler_irrigation: Highly effective on undulating semi-arid topography.

water_stress_remedy: Ensure 1st irrigation is given without fail at 30-35 DAS after completing thinning and weeding.

irrigation_methods.subsurface_or_surface_drip: Drip irrigation with 1.5 - 2.5 LPH drippers saves 50% irrigation water and increases cane yield by 25-35%.
irrigation_methods.alternate_furrow: Trash mulching in alternate furrows saves 30% water.

water_stress_remedy: Withhold irrigation 15-20 days before harvest to promote sucrose accumulation and higher brix sugar recovery.

irrigation_methods.flat_bed_irrigation: Irrigate every 5-6 days in summer and 8-10 days in winter.

water_stress_remedy: Stop irrigation 10-15 days before harvesting when 50% top neck-fall occurs to cure outer bulb scales and prevent storage rot.

water_stress_remedy: Stop irrigation 10-12 days before dehaulming/harvest to allow tuber skin to harden.

water_stress_remedy: Provide instant drainage during monsoon downpours; standing water triggers soft rot (Pythium) epidemic.
